question: In March 2025, researchers from Northwestern University identified which smartwatch- based metric as a useful predictor of cardiovascular health risks?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Daily Heart Rate Per Step (DHRPS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Daily Heart Rate Per Step (DHRPS)** is a smartwatch-based metric that tracks the relationship between an individual's heart rate and the number of steps taken daily.
 
• This metric was identified by researchers from **Northwestern University** in March 2025 as a useful predictor of **cardiovascular health risks.**
 
• The DHRPS provides insights into the **efficiency of the heart** during physical activity, helping to assess an individual's fitness levels.
 
• A higher DHRPS value may indicate potential **cardiovascular strain**, while lower values suggest better **cardiac efficiency**.
 
• This metric is particularly useful for individuals monitoring their **heart health** or engaging in fitness programs aimed at improving cardiovascular performance.
 
• The application of DHRPS can aid healthcare professionals in identifying at-risk patients and developing personalized health interventions.

__
 
• **Wearable Activity Pressure Estimate Scale (WAPES)**__

 __
 
• **WAPES** is a hypothetical metric that could potentially measure the pressure or force exerted during wearable activity.
 
• There is no established research or evidence linking WAPES to cardiovascular health prediction.
 
• It might focus more on physical exertion rather than heart-specific metrics.
 
 
 
• **Resting Pulse-to-Movement Ratio (RPMR)**__
 __
 
• **RPMR** hypothetically calculates the ratio of resting pulse rate to movement or activity levels.
 
• While it could provide insights into resting heart rate, it is not specifically identified as a predictor for cardiovascular health risks.
 
 
 
• **Weekly Step-to-Cardiac Output Index (WSCO)**__
 
 
• **WSCO** could potentially measure weekly steps in relation to cardiac output.
 
• This metric is not widely recognized in research and may focus more on general activity tracking rather than cardiovascular health risks.
